title.narrative: Mejoramiento del Acceso al Agua y Saneamiento rural y semirural en la Cuenca Alta del Río Coco

description.narrative:
The general objective of the action is to contribute to the adaptation of the vulnerable population in Nicaragua's Dry Corridor to the effects of climate change. Expected outputs include i) the protection and conservation of vulnerable water recharge areas; ii) the establishment of participatory mechanisms for the implementation of IWRM; iii) the improvement of water supply, sanitation and water harvesting infrastructure; and iv) the strengthening of the socioeconomic empowerment of women.

This action in Nicaragua's Dry Corridor aligns with climate change adaptation and mitigation, women's empowerment, and vulnerable group inclusion, adhering to international and regional sustainable development and water management objectives. It aims to significantly improve water security, boost economic activities for the vulnerable, reduce poverty, and advance gender equality in water management. The EU's role as a key partner in inclusive, sustainable development and climate justice in Nicaragua will be strengthened.

The action is linked to the New European Consensus for Development, the European Green Deal, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, and the 2020-2025 Gender Equality Strategy, and is consistent with EU guidelines on drinking water and sanitation. Regionally, it aligns with the MIP for Latin America and Central America. Globally, it supports the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda, specifically addressing SDGs 6 and 15, and contributing to SDGs 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, and 13.

The action reflects the Rio principles on climate change adaptation and mitigation through carbon sinking and markets. As a gender marker 1 project, it specifically aims to enhance women's participation and empowerment in Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), aligning with the EU's GAP III 2021-2025 in Nicaragua by increasing women's resilience to climate change and improving their decision-making on environmental issues. It embodies the "Leaving no one behind" principle by addressing climate change impacts and ensuring water rights for vulnerable populations, indigenous communities, and women in impoverished rural areas.

Building on past experiences (ALLACC I), the action prioritizes reforestation, water source protection, and community strengthening. Basin committees will be trained, and Community Water and Sanitation Committees (CAPS) with a gender focus will be strengthened to meet the needs of the most vulnerable in high-poverty, desertification-affected areas.

Project success relies on comprehensive stakeholder engagement, inclusive infrastructure development, and the empowerment of marginalized groups, especially indigenous people and women. By focusing on these elements, the project intends to improve water security, reduce climate risks, build resilience, enhance livelihoods, promote gender equity, and foster sustainable development in Nicaragua's Dry Corridor.
